data.name: Kleophan
data.gender_notes: Kleophan is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kleophan is derived from the Greek word κλεοπάτηρ (kleopatēr), which means 'glory of God'. In the Christian tradition, the name Kleophan is associated with several saints, including St. Cleophas, the brother of St. Joseph and uncle of Jesus, and St. Cleophas of Rome, a martyr under Emperor Diocletian. The name Kleophan carries the meaning “Glory of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek. Parents who choose Kleophan usually hope their child will grow to embody glory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflecting the glory of God in one's actions and character
data.etymology: Kleophan belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glory of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kleophan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: קליאופאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קליאופאן הוא שם פרטי שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'אלוהים מואיל להראות פניו' או 'אלוהים מראה פניו'. השם נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'κλέος' (כבוד) ו'φάνε' (להראות). בקונטקסט הנוצרי, השם מייצג את הרעיון של אלוהים המתגלה לבני האדם ומעניק להם כבוד והדרכה.

in_greek.name: Κλεοφάν
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός δείχνει το πρόσωπό Του
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κλεοφάν προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'κλέος' (δόξα) και 'φάνε' (να δείχνω). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει την έκφραση της θείας παρουσίας και της δόξας του Θεού. Οι πρώτοι Χριστιανοί χρησιμοποιούσαν το όνομα για να εκφράσουν την πίστη τους στην αποκάλυψη του Θεού μέσω του Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Cleophan
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Cleophan derivatur ex vocibus Graecis 'κλέος' (gloria) et 'φάνε' (ostendere). In traditione christiana, nomen hoc significat revelationem Dei et manifestationem gloriae eius. Quod nomen olim a primis Christianis adhibebatur ad exprimendam fidem in Deum, qui se revelavit per Jesum Christum.

in_english.name: Kleophan
in_english.meaning: Glorious manifestation of God, God shows His face
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kleophan originates from Greek roots 'κλέος' (glory) and 'φάνε' (to show). It signifies the glorious manifestation of God or God's revelation of His face to humanity. In Christian tradition, Kleophan represents the concept of divine disclosure and the glory of God made manifest through Jesus Christ. Historically, the name has been associated with spiritual illumination and guidance. Today, Kleophan is used across various Christian cultures to symbolize a deep connection with the divine.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kleophan holds cultural significance as a tribute to the early Christian saints named Cleophas. It reflects the deep-rooted history and traditions of the Christian faith. The name Kleophan can be considered a reminder of the strong influence and impact that the Christian faith has had on human history and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Kleophan lies in its meaning 'glory of God'. It is a constant reminder of the ultimate purpose and goal of life, which is to bring glory to God. The name Kleophan inspires a sense of reverence, devotion, and commitment to living a life that honors and glorifies God. It also serves as a reminder of the saints who lived purposeful and pious lives, inspiring generations to do the same.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kleophas (or Kleophan), in Greek, means "glory of God's face." This name signifies the deep connection between the individual and the divine, reminding us of the inherent dignity and holiness bestowed upon every person by God. It also underscores the importance of seeking God's presence in our lives, allowing His light to illuminate our paths.

historical_references.reference: Kleophas, a disciple of Saint Peter, is mentioned in the New Testament (Matthew 27:56, Mark 15:40, and Luke 24:51). He is listed among the Galilean followers of Jesus who were present at the crucifixion, the burial, and the resurrection.

Kleophas, also known as Cleophas or Alpheus, is mentioned in the Gospel of John (19:25) as the father of James the Less, one of the brothers of Jesus. This reference is less certain as it does not appear in the Synoptic Gospels.

modern_usage.modern_context: Kleophan, an ancient Greek name meaning 'glory of Phoebus', has seen a modern revival in various contexts. In Reddit communities dedicated to Greek mythology, users often discuss and role-play Kleophan as a character. On Goodreads, historical fiction novels featuring Kleophan as a main character can be found. In tabletop gaming communities, Kleophan is a popular name for player-created characters in mythology-themed campaigns.
